From Bellingham, drive SR-542 east about 55 miles to the end of the highway. At Heather Meadows go one-way around Picture Lake past the ski lifts; the large parking area is at the end of the road on the right. The highway is plowed only to Heather Meadows outside roughly July to late September.
From Glacier, drive SR 542 east about 24 miles to the end of the highway at the large Artist Point parking lot.

From Port Angeles, take Race Street south onto Hurricane Ridge Road and climb to the Hurricane Ridge parking area; turn sharply left onto the gravel Obstruction Point Road and follow it about 8 miles to its end at the trailhead. The gravel road is generally open only from mid-July to October.

From the Obstruction Point Trailhead (6,150 ft) - reached via the narrow, unpaved Obstruction Point Road that branches off Hurricane Ridge Road just below Hurricane Ridge - follow the Grand Pass Trail as it climbs onto and traverses Lillian Ridge.
From Stevens Pass, drive US-2 east 11.3 miles and turn north onto FR-657, signed for Merritt Lake. Follow it 1.6 miles to the road's end and trailhead parking.

From US-2 near milepost 76 (about 11.5 miles east of Stevens Pass / 24 miles west of Leavenworth), turn onto Forest Road 657 (rough, high-clearance recommended) and drive 1.5 miles to the Merritt Lake Trailhead (3,050 ft).

Hoh Rain Forest Trailhead (Hoh River Trail)

approach_logistics.trailheadDirection: From the Shannon Ridge Trailhead at the end of FR-1152-014 (~2,500 ft) off Baker Lake Road

From Sedro-Woolley, drive SR-20 east to milepost 82 and turn left (north) onto the Baker Lake Highway (FR-11). Go 24 miles to FR-1152, directly across from Shannon Creek Campground, turn left and go 4.5 miles to FR-1152014, then turn right and go 1.5 miles to the road's end.

From I-90 take Exit 32, turn left onto 436th Ave SE and follow it to SE North Bend Way; turn left, then after 0.3 mile turn right onto SE Mount Si Road and continue 2.4 miles to the trailhead entrance on the left.

From I-90 take Exit 32, turn left onto 436th Ave SE and follow it to SE North Bend Way; turn left, then after 0.3 mile turn right onto SE Mount Si Road and continue 2.4 miles to the trailhead entrance on the left.

The standard-route trailhead is the Putvin Trailhead (Trail #813) on Hamma Hamma Road (FR-25), about 11.8-12.1 miles west of Hwy 101 and about 4.5 miles past the Lena Lake trailhead, at roughly 1,600 ft elevation.

approach_logistics.trailhead: Mount Teneriffe Trailhead (SE Mount Si Road)
approach_logistics.trailheadDirection: From I-90 exit 32, turn left on 436th Avenue SE and go about 0.5 mile to SE North Bend Way, turn left, and after about 0.25 mile turn right onto SE Mount Si Road. Follow it 2.9 miles, past the Little Si and Mount Si trailheads, to the lot on the left.

From I-90 exit 32, turn left on 436th Avenue SE and go about 0.5 mile to SE North Bend Way, turn left, and after about 0.25 mile turn right onto SE Mount Si Road. Follow it 2.9 miles, past the Little Si and Mount Si trailheads, to the lot on the left.

From Winthrop, head north on East Chewuch River Road for 6.5 miles and turn right onto FR-37. Follow FR-37 for 13 miles, then turn left onto FR-39 and continue 7.5 miles to Tiffany Springs Campground.

From Winthrop, head north on East Chewuch River Road for 6.5 miles and turn right onto FR-37. Follow FR-37 for 13 miles, then turn left onto FR-39 and continue 7.5 miles to Tiffany Springs Campground.

approach_logistics.trailhead: Mt. Baker Ski Area upper lot (Bagley Lakes Trailhead)
approach_logistics.trailheadDirection: From Glacier, drive Mount Baker Highway (SR 542) east to the upper Mt. Baker Ski Area parking lot at the Bagley Lakes Trailhead, milepost 54.6. The highway is gated here for the season and has been closed beyond since October 25, 2026, so this is where cars stop in winter; in summer the road continues to the Artist Point lot.

approach_logistics.trailhead: Mt. Baker Ski Area upper lot (Bagley Lakes Trailhead)
approach_logistics.trailheadDirection: From Glacier, drive Mount Baker Highway (SR 542) east to the upper Mt. Baker Ski Area parking lot at the Bagley Lakes Trailhead, milepost 54.6. The highway is gated here for the season and has been closed beyond since October 25, 2026, so this is where cars stop in winter; in summer the road continues to the Artist Point lot.

Mount Shark Road end near Mount Engadine Lodge

approach_logistics.trailheadDirection: From Leavenworth, drive US Highway 2 west approximately 17.4-17.7 miles (or from Stevens Pass, drive east about 18 miles) to just past the Nason Creek Rest Area.

From Mazama, head north on Lost River Road and after about 9 miles turn right onto FR-5400. Climb about 8.7 miles to Harts Pass; the road is narrow and rugged, suited to high-clearance vehicles only, and is typically open July through September.

approach_logistics.trailhead: "Rainy Pass Picnic Area / Lake Ann Trailhead (SR-20)"
approach_logistics.trailheadDirection: From Marblemount, drive SR-20 east about 50 miles to Rainy Pass; the picnic area and Lake Ann trailhead lot is on the south side of the highway.

From Highway 2 on the west side of Leavenworth, turn south onto Icicle Road and drive 8.4 miles, then turn left onto Forest Road 7601 (Eightmile Road, washboard and potholed) and go 3.1 miles to the Eightmile trailhead parking.

approach_logistics.trailhead: Rainy Pass / Lake Ann–Maple Pass Trailhead
approach_logistics.trailheadDirection: From the paved pullout at Rainy Pass (4,855 ft) on SR-20 — signed 'Rainy Pass Trailhead,' 52 miles east of Marblemount, right where the PCT crosses the highway — start on the Lake Ann/Maple Pass Trail (well-graded, heavily used).

From the West Fork Buttermilk Trailhead (elev. ~3,960 ft, at the end of FR-4300-500 off East Buttermilk Creek Road/FR-43, reached via Twisp River Road west of Twisp), follow the West Fork Buttermilk Trail #411 into the Lake Chelan-Sawtooth Wilderness.
From Winthrop, drive west on SR-20 about 27 miles (about 4 miles east of Washington Pass), turn right onto Forest Road 400, and follow it about 1 mile to the trailhead parking.
From Diablo (SR-20 milepost 126): park near the pool building; the Sourdough Mountain Trail starts behind it (~900 ft)

From the Nisqually Entrance of Mount Rainier National Park, drive to Longmire, pass the National Park Inn and turn right at the two-story building with the flagpole. Continue straight through the employee housing area and across the suspension bridge, which has a 3-ton vehicle limit; the trailhead is 300 feet past the bridge and parking is limited.
From the De Roux trailhead and campground on FR-9737, via the Boulder-De Roux Trail #1392 west up the valley to its last switchback

approach_logistics.trailhead: Frenchman Coulee parking on Vantage Road
approach_logistics.trailheadDirection: From Seattle take Interstate 90 east over the Columbia River past Vantage to exit 143, turn left onto Silica Road, pass beneath the freeway, then turn left at the first chance onto Vantage Road and follow it 1.4 miles down the canyon to parking on the left. A Discover Pass is required. Since May 2026 rockslides have closed Vantage Road, so the parking cannot be reached by car; check the road status before you go.

Drive to the Conrad Meadows / South Fork Tieton Trailhead (Trail #1120, elev. ~4,044 ft): from Naches, WA take US-12 W about 22 miles, turn onto Forest Road 1200 (Tieton Reservoir Road) for 4.5 miles, then onto Forest Road 1000 (South Fork Tieton Road) for 12.6 miles to the trailhead at road's end (last ~7 miles gravel, generally in good condition).

From Glacier, drive Mt. Baker Highway (SR 542) east about 1 mile past the Glacier Public Service Center to Glacier Creek Road (Forest Road 39), turn right, then take an immediate left onto Deadhorse Road (Forest Road 37) and follow it 12.7 miles to the trailhead at the end of the road. Since June 2026 Deadhorse Road has been closed at its start until further notice while flood damage is repaired; check the road status before you go.

From Carleton, drive SR-153 south 1.4 miles, turn right onto Libby Creek Road for 2.5 miles, then left onto FR-43 for 5.1 miles. Turn left onto FR-4340 for 1.2 miles, right onto FR-700 for 1.5 miles, and left onto FR-750 for 0.9 mile to the trailhead.

approach_logistics.trailhead: Hannegan Trailhead / Campground (Hannegan Pass Road, FR 32)
approach_logistics.trailheadDirection: From Mount Baker Highway (SR-542), about 12.5 miles east of the Glacier Public Service Center, turn left onto Hannegan Pass Road (FR-32) and drive about 5.3 miles to the road-end trailhead.
From US 2 at Skykomish, south on Foss River Road (FR 68), then left on FR 6835 for its last 1.9 miles to the West Fork Foss trailhead (~1,650 ft).

From Seattle take I-90 east to Exit 54 for Hyak and turn right onto WA-906; it bends left almost at once, so turn left to keep on WA-906, then after about 0.4 miles turn right into the Hyak Sno-Park (winter parking needs a daily fee or seasonal Sno-Park permit).

From Newhalem, drive SR-20 east 42.1 miles; the trailhead is on the south side of the highway just before Washington Pass Overlook. From Winthrop it is 31.3 miles west, a little under a mile past the overlook. SR-20 closes for winter.
From the Old Lake Valhalla/Lake Janus Trailhead on Smith Brook Road (~4,150 ft)
From I-90 take Exit 47 for Denny Creek and follow Forest Road 58 to the three Denny Creek parking lots, about half a mile past the campground (Northwest Forest Pass or Sno-Park permit).
From Trout Lake, drive FR-23 north about 24 miles to the junction with FR-2329, signed for Takhlakh Lake Campground. Follow FR-2329 past the campground for about 4.5 miles to the trailhead.

From Trout Lake, drive Mount Adams Road north to the V intersection with FR-23, veer right and go about 1 mile, then turn left onto FR-80 (signed South Climb) and follow it to its end. Turn right onto FR-8040 and drive north past Morrison Creek Campground to the old Cold Springs Camp; the last 3 miles are very rough and narrow.

From Trout Lake, drive north on Mount Adams Road to the V intersection with Forest Road 23, veer right and go about 1 mile, then turn left onto Forest Road 80 (signed South Climb) and follow it to its end. Turn right onto Forest Road 8040 and drive north past Morrison Creek Campground to the trailhead; the last 3 miles are very rough and narrow.

approach_logistics.trailhead: Hurricane Ridge Visitor Center (High Ridge Trail)
approach_logistics.trailheadDirection: From US-101 in Port Angeles, head south on Race Street for 1.2 miles to Hurricane Ridge Road, then drive about 17.5 miles uphill to the visitor center lot.

From SR-20 just past milepost 82, turn north onto Baker Lake Road and follow it about 12 miles, turn left onto FR-12, and after about 3.5 miles turn right onto FR-13, which runs to the trailhead parking at its end.

approach_logistics.trailhead: Cathedral Rock / Deception Pass Trailhead (Tucquala Meadows)
approach_logistics.trailheadDirection: From Roslyn, follow SR 903 north about 14.8 miles to the end of the maintained road, bear right onto Forest Road 4330, and continue on gravel to the trailhead at its end.

From the Upper Trailhead (elev. ~3,500 ft, at the end of FS Road 2419-014 off FS 24/FS 2419 - the lot has a vault toilet, picnic table, and requires a Northwest Forest Pass), Trail #812 climbs immediately.
Start from the Bagley Lakes Trailhead (~4,200 ft) at the south end of the upper Mt. Baker Ski Area parking lot near the Heather Meadows Visitor Center.

approach_logistics.trailhead: North Fork Quinault Trailhead / Ranger Station
approach_logistics.trailheadDirection: From US-101 at milepost 126, turn onto South Shore Road and follow it 12.9 miles to the Quinault River bridge; cross it, turn right onto North Shore Road, and drive 3.5 miles to the road end at the trailhead and ranger station.

From Granite Falls, take Quarry Road about 4 miles to the Mountain Loop Highway, turn left and go 10 miles to Verlot, continue 1 mile and turn right onto Mount Pilchuck Road, then follow FR-42 for 6.8 miles to the trailhead lot.
From Darrington, turn right onto the Mountain Loop Highway and drive 12.5 miles to the signed turnoff on the left, then turn left onto FR-2095 and go 1.5 miles to the trailhead on the right.
Via the Elwha Valley: Olympic Hot Springs Road is closed to vehicles at Madison Falls — walk or bike ~6-7 miles to the Whiskey Bend Trailhead

From the Climbers Bivouac trailhead (3,700 ft, the highest vehicle access on this side of the mountain, reached via FR-90/FR-83/FR-81/FR-830 from Cougar), the route starts on the signed Ptarmigan Trail #216A through open forest.

From Cougar, drive east on Lewis River Road, which becomes Forest Road 90, to the junction with Forest Road 83; turn left and go about 6 miles to the Marble Mountain Sno-Park. Forest Road 83 is gated at the sno-park in winter and early spring.

approach_logistics.trailhead: Hoh Rain Forest Visitor Center / Hoh River Trailhead
approach_logistics.trailheadDirection: From Forks, drive US-101 south about 13 miles and turn east onto Upper Hoh Road. Follow it about 18 miles to the visitor center and trailhead at the end of the road.

Start at the Mt. Townsend Upper Trailhead (elev. ~3,300 ft), reached via Forest Road 27 off Penny Creek Road out of Quilcene - the trailhead has a small gravel lot and a Buckhorn Wilderness boundary sign where Trail #839 begins.
Start at the Tubal Cain Trailhead (elev. ~3,300 ft, reached via FR 2870/2880), and follow the Tubal Cain Trail #840 (Copper Creek drainage) south.

Start at the Stafford Creek Trailhead (Trail #1359), Cle Elum Ranger District, Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest, at the end of Stafford Creek Road (FR 9703), which leaves North Fork Teanaway River Road (FR 9737) past 29 Pines Campground - a small, often-overflowing lot for roughly 20 cars (Northwest Forest Pass required).
Park at the Eagle Creek/Oval trailhead (~3,000 ft) at the end of FR 4420-080, reached via Twisp River Road/FR 44 (~12.5 mi west of Twisp) and the West Buttermilk/FR 4420 spur.

approach_logistics.trailhead: Hannegan Pass Trailhead (end of Ruth Creek Rd / FR-32), via Hannegan Pass, Chilliwack River Trail, Whatcom Pass and Perfect Pass to the SW side of Phantom Peak
approach_logistics.trailheadDirection: From the Mount Baker Highway (SR-542), turn onto Hannegan Pass Road (FR-32) and drive 5.3 miles to the trailhead at the end of the road

From Elbe, drive SR-706 east through Ashford to the Nisqually Entrance of the park, then continue about 6.5 miles to Longmire. The center is in the Longmire Administration Building, across from the museum.

From the Reynolds Creek Trailhead (~3,100-3,170 ft, reached via Forest Road 4435, which crosses the Twisp River near Mystery Campground before the Spur 4435-015 turnoff to the trailhead), the route follows Reynolds Creek Trail #402, an unmaintained, primitive Forest Service trail entering the Lake Chelan-Sawtooth Wilderness.

From the Rock Mountain Trail #1587 pullout on US-2 (small dirt lot on the north side of the highway near the powerlines, no facilities), the trail launches immediately uphill on what was formerly a service road.

From Sedro-Woolley, drive WA-9 north to Acme, turn right (east) onto Mosquito Lake Road and follow it about 9 miles, cross the Middle Fork Nooksack River and continue onto Forest Road 38 for about 11 miles to the Elbow Lake trailhead. Since July 2026 Forest Road 38 has been closed to vehicles by a washout at milepost 7.

Trailhead is the West Fork Buttermilk Creek Trailhead (Trail #411), reached via Twisp River Road ~10.7-10.8 miles from Twisp, then left on Buttermilk Creek Road, staying left onto East Buttermilk Road (Forest Road 43) for roughly 4 miles, then right onto the Road 500 spur for about 2.7 miles to the road-end trailhead at about 3,960 ft.

Drive Hwy 101 to just before Sequim Bay State Park, turn onto Louella Rd, then Palo Alto Rd (becomes FR 28) for about 6 miles, turn right on FR 2880 along the Dungeness River, then in 1.7 miles turn left on FR 2870 and continue roughly 6.5-9 miles (gravel, winds steeply down to a river crossing) to the large Dungeness/Royal Basin trailhead lot (picnic table, vault toilet).
From the Foggy Dew Trailhead (3,400 ft)

From Glacier, drive east on Mount Baker Highway (SR 542) for about 12 miles and turn left onto Twin Lakes Road (FR 3065) at the end of the maintenance facility. Follow it about 4.5 miles to the trailhead parking.

From Bellingham, drive SR-542 east about 46 miles, which is 13 miles past Glacier, and just before the third crossing of the Nooksack River turn left onto FR-32, then follow it 5.3 miles to its end at Hannegan Campground, where the trailhead is.

From Loomis, take County Road #9425 north 2 miles to County Road #4066/FR-39; follow FR-39 about 14 miles, then turn onto FR-3900-500 and follow it about 6 miles (high-clearance vehicle recommended, not advised for passenger cars) to the Iron Gate Trailhead.

From Loomis, drive north on County Road 9425 for about 2 miles, then turn west onto County Road 4066, which becomes FR-39, and follow it about 20 miles to Long Swamp Campground, where the trailhead is.

From Loomis, drive north on County Road 9425 for 2 miles, turn west onto County Road 4066, which becomes Forest Road 39, and follow it about 20 miles to Long Swamp Campground. Continue about 3 miles on Forest Road 3900-300 to the Cathedral Driveway trailhead.
Park at the Thirtymile Trailhead (~3,400 ft) at the end of West Chewuch Road, about 29 miles north of Winthrop.
